entries.title: Canvas writes return 422 while reads succeed (missing or invalid CSRF token)
entries.root_cause: Verified live 2026-09-22: Canvas returns exactly this generic body when a non-GET request arrives without a valid X-CSRF-Token. Reproduced on demand with absent header and with deliberately wrong token, byte-identical bodies. The most likely probe-side cause is harvesting the token from the csrf-token meta tag, which the tenant homepage currently does not have (verified live), so the header is never sent.
entries.is_not: This is not Canvas blocking writes, not rate limiting (rate-limit headers showed a full bucket, no 429s, no Retry-After), not session death (a dead session 302s API calls instead of 422), not a write halt (write_halt_active was false), and not a tenant-side change (tenant changes return 401 or 403 with specific messages, and writes work again with zero config changes once the token is sent).
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried {operation} on {tenant}, and every write came back with an HTTP 422 (unprocessable_content) while reads kept working fine. What the evidence showed: your sign-in is healthy and the rate limit is untouched, so this is not a broken session. Canvas is asking for a security token (X-CSRF-Token) that the request did not carry, which is the standard missing-or-invalid-token response, reproduced exactly with absent and wrong tokens. What this means: your Canvas session is fine and nothing on your side changed; the request just needs to carry a fresh token, which the normal write path fetches automatically on each call. What happens next: I am resending through the normal page-context path, which fetches a fresh token per call, and verifying with a readback.
entries.auto_action: Retry the write through the canonical page-context path with a fresh _csrf_token cookie harvest per call, then run a terminal readback to confirm the write landed.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate only if the canonical path also 422s with a confirmed token harvest, and include the x-request-context-id so it can go to Instructure; that combination was never observed in the audit.
entries.signature_notes: affects: "every non-GET regardless of encoding (JSON, form-encoded, PUT, UI route)"; body_contains: "unprocessable_content"; http_status: 422; rate_limit_remaining: ">0 (bucket full, e.g. 700.0)"; reads_ok: true; retry_after_header: "absent"; session_health: "logged_in=true, keepalive healthy"; writes_fail: true

entries.title: Write refused before sending: no _csrf_token in the live browser session
entries.root_cause: The page-context write path harvests the X-CSRF-Token fresh from the _csrf_token cookie on every call. When the live document.cookie has no _csrf_token (helper tab navigated away, cookie expired, or session otherwise degraded), the write is refused before any network call. This is the fail-closed fix for the 2026-09-22 incident where missing tokens produced misleading provider 422s; the product path can no longer produce a silent missing-token write.
entries.is_not: This is not a provider refusal: no HTTP request was sent, so there is no 422 and nothing was applied. It is not session death either (a dead session redirects API calls to the login page); it is specifically the CSRF cookie missing from a live page.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation}. What the evidence showed: the browser refused to send the write because the live page had no _csrf_token cookie, so no CSRF header could be built. No request reached Canvas and nothing was applied. What this means: the helper browser session is degraded (the tab may have navigated away or the cookie expired); the Canvas sign-in itself is not proven broken. What happens next: I am re-checking the helper session and re-harvesting the token from the live page, then resending the write through the normal page-context path.
entries.auto_action: Verify the helper session is alive and the tenant tab is open, re-harvest _csrf_token from the live document.cookie, and resend the write through the canonical page-context path.
entries.escalate_when: the helper session is healthy and the tenant tab is open but document.cookie still has no _csrf_token
entries.signature_notes: fail-closed pre-send refusal raised by transport/local_chromium.py (CsrfTokenMissing) or transport/browser_backend.py (BrowserCsrfTokenMissing); no provider contact happened

What happens next: I am checking the session and resending through the normal page-context path with a fresh token harvest, then verifying with a readback.

entries.title: Canvas 429 rate limiting
entries.root_cause: Verified mechanism: Canvas's rate limiter answered 429 with the bucket exhausted. Distinguishing evidence from the 422-CSRF failure: the 429 carries x-rate-limit-remaining at 0.0 and a Retry-After header, while the CSRF 422 carries a full bucket (700.0) and no Retry-After.
entries.is_not: This is not a write block, not a CSRF problem, and not session death. The tiebreaker against the 422 CSRF mode: check x-rate-limit-remaining and the presence of Retry-After before classifying.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried {operation} on {tenant} and Canvas answered 429, its polite way of saying too many requests at once. What the evidence showed: the rate-limit bucket at zero and a Retry-After instruction, so this is confirmed throttling, not a broken session or a blocked write. What this means: the request is valid but needs to wait its turn. What happens next: I am honoring Canvas's Retry-After and retrying automatically; writes that were in flight are recorded as uncertain and I will verify with a readback before reporting success.
entries.auto_action: Backoff for the Retry-After duration and retry. Reads retry up to 4 times; writes convert to UncertainWrite and get reconciled by readback.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate if 429s persist across several backoff cycles on low-volume traffic, which would suggest a tenant-side policy change rather than normal throttling.
entries.signature_notes: http_status: 429; rate_limit_remaining: "0.0"; reads_behavior: "retried up to 4 times then fail"; retry_after_header: "present (honored)"; writes_behavior: "become UncertainWrite immediately, Retry-After honored"

entries.title: Canvas session died (login page returned, SessionDead)
entries.root_cause: Verified mechanism: the provider's session cookie expired, was revoked, or the SSO flow lapsed, so the tenant answers with its login page (redirect or HTTP 200 HTML). The transport detects both shapes and raises SessionDead. Expiry is never warned ahead of time: the keepalive watches process health and the URL heuristic, never the expiry horizon (known real horizons included a stay-signed-in credential expiring 2026-10-05 and an OTP remember-me expiring 2026-10-21), so the first signal is a failed op.
entries.is_not: This is not a write block and not rate limiting. A dead Chromium masquerades similarly but shows url='' with logged_in=false and needs a browser restart, not a sign-in.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried {operation} on {tenant} and Canvas answered with its login page instead of data, which means your saved sign-in has expired. What the evidence showed: a redirect to /login (or login HTML returned with a 200 status), the standard signature of a dead session. What this means: your Canvas login in the helper browser needs to be refreshed; nothing about the operation itself failed. What happens next: I am pausing all writes so nothing goes out while the session is dead, holding any unfinished work aside, and asking you to sign in once through the helper page. After I verify the fresh sign-in, the held work needs your explicit approval before anything re-runs.
entries.auto_action: Halt writes via the write-halt lever, quarantine in-flight ops, and require a guided re-sign-in with principal re-verification before any op resumes. Nothing re-dispatches without educator approval.
entries.escalate_when: Always bring this to the educator: only they can re-sign in, and only they can approve the resume of quarantined ops.
entries.signature_notes: http_status_variants: ["302 to /login", "200 with login HTML in body (content sniff raises SessionDead)"]; reads_behavior: "fail as SessionDead; pre-hardening reads journaled the login page as success"; status_endpoint: "logged_in=false"; writes_behavior: "UncertainWrite if a write was attempted, otherwise nothing journaled"

entries.title: Session died mid-write, effect state unknown (UncertainWrite)
entries.root_cause: Verified mechanism: the session died between dispatch and the provider's answer, so the transport cannot prove whether Canvas applied the write. The write-integrity hardening (wave 2) classifies this as UncertainWrite rather than retrying blindly, which would risk a double-apply.
entries.is_not: This is not a confirmed failure and not a confirmed success. Treating it as either is how silent double-applies happened before the hardening.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried {operation} on {tenant} and the session died right in the middle of the write, so I cannot tell from the transport alone whether Canvas applied it. What the evidence showed: an UncertainWrite record in the journal with the attempt details kept, which is the honest classification the system uses instead of guessing. What this means: the write may or may not have landed, and retrying blindly could create a duplicate. What happens next: I am running a terminal readback against Canvas to see whether the object exists as written; if it did not land, I will re-dispatch under a fresh claim, and if it did, I will report it done with the evidence.
entries.auto_action: Reconcile via terminal readback (member GET, list readback). If the write did not land, re-dispatch only after the session is healthy; never retry the ambiguous write blindly.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate if the readback cannot decide the state (provider gives no listable signal), so the educator can check the object in the Canvas UI before any re-dispatch.
entries.signature_notes: classification: "UncertainWrite"; journal: "audit record journaled under a fresh event id with the step evidence retained"; verify_path: "terminal readback (list the object, read the member GET) decides applied vs not-applied"

entries.title: Canvas soft-delete: DELETE returns 200 but the object still reads back 200
entries.root_cause: Verified live 2026-09-22 on a classic quiz: Canvas returned 200 to two DELETEs and direct GET still returned 200 afterward, yet the quiz was absent from the course listing (66 listed), its backing assignment 404d, and its questions list was empty. This is provider-side soft-delete behavior, not a failed delete.
entries.is_not: This is not a failed deletion and not a permission problem. Re-issuing DELETEs does not help.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I deleted {object} on {tenant} and Canvas confirmed with a 200, but a direct fetch of the object still returns 200. What the evidence showed: the object is gone from the course listing, its backing assignment returns 404, and its questions list is empty, which is Canvas's soft-delete behavior on this object type: functionally deleted in every user-visible sense while the direct fetch still answers. What this means: the delete worked and no further action is needed. What happens next: I am recording the absence evidence in the receipt and moving on rather than re-issuing the delete.
entries.auto_action: Accept the deletion after verifying absence through the course listing, the backing assignment, and the questions list. Do not re-issue the DELETE.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate only if the object is still user-visible (in the course listing or functional), which would indicate the delete genuinely did not take.

entries.title: Helper server not running
entries.root_cause: Verified: the helper is supervised every 5 minutes, by a cron entry where the machine has cron, or by the keepalive background loop (helper/supervisor.py) where it does not (the Muse VM has no cron daemon). After a restart the helper stays down until that supervision runs keepalive; on a machine without cron the background loop starts again only with `bin/morrow start` or the next morrow command.
entries.is_not: This is not session death; there is no browser to check yet.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried to reach the login helper and it is not running. What the evidence showed: a connection refusal on its local port. After a restart the helper stays down until its supervision (a cron entry, or the keepalive background loop on a machine without cron) runs again. What this means: nothing about your Canvas session; the local service just is not up. What happens next: I am starting it through the keepalive supervisor and then checking the session health; if it comes up logged in, we continue where we left off.
entries.auto_action: Run helper/keepalive.sh to relaunch, then run bin/morrow start so supervision keeps it up (it starts the keepalive background loop on a machine without cron and is a no-op with cron), then re-probe /status and session health.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate if the helper fails to come up after keepalive recovery (log the real failure from server.log), since a human may need to re-sign in.
entries.signature_notes: evidence: transport/chromium_session.py _ensure_transport raises ExecutorError('chromium backend: browser unavailable (...); the login helper endpoint is down too -- start it with helper/keepalive.sh, then retry') when the browser launch fails and the helper /status endpoint is unreachable. Previous signature keyed on 'helper_reachable', which no production code ever sets, so the entry could never match (2026-09-22 first-run audit).

entries.title: A different Canvas account is signed in to the helper
entries.root_cause: Verified mechanism: before every write, and once per session for reads, the Chromium lane reads GET /api/v1/users/self and compares it with the account pinned at first sign-in (reauth/state_machine.py pin). Someone signed in to the helper browser as another account (a shared machine, a second educator, a student), so the lane refused and imposed the re-auth write halt.

entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried {operation} through the login helper. What the evidence showed: the helper browser is signed in to a different Canvas account than the one this connector is pinned to. What this means: nothing was sent, and writes are paused so nothing can go out under the wrong account. What happens next: please sign out in the helper page and sign back in with your own account; I will then confirm it is your pinned account and resume. If you want to use a different account from now on, I can disconnect this connector first so you can sign in fresh.

The fix adds a chromium_alive field so this state is treated as recoverable (restart) instead of signed-out.

entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I stopped {operation} before it reached Canvas because the call was declared as a read while the catalog says it is a write. What the evidence showed: the mismatch between what the call claimed (for example, 'read') and what the operation actually does (a write). What this means: the approval step required for writes would have been skipped, so the system refused rather than proceed ungoverned. What happens next: I am re-declaring the operation as a write and running it through the full approval step.
entries.auto_action: Derive the effect class from the catalog, never from the caller; re-run the admission path correctly.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate to engineering if the catalog's own R/W marking is wrong, since that is a data fix, not an educator decision.
entries.signature_notes: evidence: "W3-P0-6 catalog path fixed; W4-P0-10 manifest path: effects read/plan bypassed every write safeguard pre-fix"; gate: "CatalogEffectMismatch"; trigger: "caller declared a write as read (or a manifest effects field set to read/plan for a write block)"

entries.title: Quarantine op_id collision: one approval re-arms many ops (pre-fix)
entries.root_cause: Verified pre-fix: epoch-second default op_ids collided under burst quarantine, and approve_op flipped every ledger entry whose op_id matched, so approving one paused op silently approved dozens of others, including destructive writes quarantined after session death.
entries.is_not: This is not educator error; the identifier scheme made distinct ops indistinguishable.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I set several operations aside after the session died, and before approving any resume I checked their identities. What the evidence showed: the old bookkeeping could mix up held operations with each other, so approving one could have silently approved others, including destructive ones. What this means: resume approvals cannot be trusted until each operation has its own identity. What happens next: I am re-holding them under the fixed scheme and asking you to approve each operation individually, showing you exactly what each one is.
entries.auto_action: Re-issue quarantine entries with unique ids; require per-op educator approval; never bulk-approve.
entries.escalate_when: Always: resume of quarantined ops is an educator approval by design.
entries.signature_notes: evidence: "W5-P0-1 (resource), fixed 2026-09-22"; fixed: "default op_id is uuid4 (or ns-timestamp + PID); 100 rapid quarantines produce 100 distinct ids"; pre_fix: "default op_id op-<epoch-seconds>; 40 rapid quarantines produced only 2 distinct ids; approving one flipped 28 actions to approved"

entries.title: Journal torn line detected (fail-closed, no silent skip)
entries.root_cause: Verified: pre-fix the journal skipped torn lines, so a crash-torn tail forgot the op_id and allowed replay. Post-fix, torn lines are a loud failure.
entries.is_not: This is not normal operation and not something to work around by hand-editing the journal.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried to continue {operation} and found the operation log was damaged by a crash. What the evidence showed: the log's own integrity check failing loudly, which is the designed behavior: it refuses to guess rather than risk replaying a write. What this means: work is paused until the log is repaired, because proceeding could apply a write twice. What happens next: I am not touching the log by hand; this needs the journal repair procedure run deliberately, and I will report exactly what it finds.
entries.auto_action: Stop dispatch; surface the journal-repair procedure to the operator. Never hand-edit the journal.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate to engineering immediately: journal integrity is a stop-everything event.
entries.signature_notes: detector: "JournalTorn raised on unparseable lines"; evidence: "W2-P0-3, proven live pre-fix, fixed post-wave-2"; fixed_behavior: "torn lines fail loudly; op_id never silently forgotten; exclusive flock on checks and mutations; fsync on writes"

entries.title: Ambiguous write failure (UncertainWrite, no blind retry)
entries.root_cause: Verified (W2-P0-1, proven live): a connection reset after the provider applied a write is indistinguishable from one before it, so blind retry double-applies. Post-fix, ambiguous failures raise UncertainWrite instead of retrying.
entries.is_not: This is not a confirmed failure and not a success. It is the honest third state.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried {operation} and the connection broke at a point where I cannot tell whether Canvas applied the write. What the evidence showed: the ambiguous transport failure, and the system recorded it as uncertain rather than retrying blindly, because a blind retry once double-applied a write live. What this means: the write may have landed exactly once, and guessing either way is how duplicates happen. What happens next: I am reconciling with a terminal readback to learn the true state; only if the write provably did not land will I send it again, under a fresh claim.
entries.auto_action: Reconcile via readback; re-dispatch only on proven non-application.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate if the readback cannot decide the state; the educator can check the object in the Canvas UI.
entries.signature_notes: classification: "UncertainWrite"; fixed_behavior: "never retried blindly; pre-fix retries double-applied non-idempotent POSTs (proven live)"; journal: "fsync'd write-ahead pending record before dispatch; uncertain receipt journaled with step evidence"; triggers: ["connection reset where the server may have applied the write", "HTTP 429/5xx on a write", "ambiguous transport failure"]

entries.title: Write returned success but its readback could not confirm it (UncertainWrite)
entries.root_cause: Verified mechanism: every write is read back with a fresh GET and compared field by field. When that GET itself fails (HTTP 429 or 5xx, a transport error, or an answer that is not an object) after Canvas answered the write with success, the executor cannot prove the stored values either way, so it journals the op as uncertain instead of failed.
entries.is_not: This is not a failed write and not a confirmed success. Canvas accepted the write; only the check afterward did not complete.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried {operation}. What the evidence showed: Canvas answered the write with success, but when I read the object back to check it, that read did not complete (reference {correlation_id}), so I could not confirm what was stored. What this means: the change most likely landed, but it is unconfirmed, not a failure, and sending it again could make a duplicate. What happens next: I will read the object again to confirm it, and I will not resend the write unless that read proves it did not land.
entries.auto_action: Journal as uncertain; reconcile with a fresh readback of the written object; never blind-retry the write.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate if repeated readbacks cannot confirm the object, so the educator can check it in the Canvas UI.
entries.signature_notes: exception: "UncertainWrite" raised by dispatch/executor.py dispatch_entry when run_write_readback's GET fails after a 2xx write; journal: verification "uncertain", uncertain=true.

entries.title: Write returned success but its declared check proved a different result (VerificationFailed)
entries.root_cause: Verified mechanism: a write that declares a verify block is read back after Canvas answers with success, and the readback is compared with what the write asked for. When that readback completes and proves the stored object differs (a field has another value, or the object is missing), the executor journals the op as failed, not uncertain, and raises VerificationFailed naming the mismatch.
entries.is_not: This is not an uncertain write: the readback completed and proved the result differs. It is not a success either, and it is not a session or network problem.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried {operation}. What the evidence showed: Canvas answered the write with success, but when I read the object back to check it, the result did not match what the write asked for (reference {correlation_id}); the journal records the mismatch as a failed write. What this means: the change did not land as intended, so I am treating it as failed, not done. What happens next: I will show you what Canvas actually has next to what was requested, and you decide whether I correct it, remove it, or leave it as it is.
entries.auto_action: Record as a failed write; never report success; present the requested vs stored values and the object address; never blind-retry.
entries.escalate_when: Always surface to the educator with the mismatch; they choose correct, remove, or keep.
entries.signature_notes: exception: "VerificationFailed" raised by dispatch/executor.py dispatch_entry when a declared verify block's readback completed and proved a mismatch (the proven branch); journal: verification "failed". An unproven readback raises UncertainWrite instead (write-readback-unconfirmed).

entries.title: Write never reached the provider (WriteNotAttempted, safe to retry)
entries.root_cause: Verified in code (dispatch/executor.py): only failures that prove the provider never saw the request bytes retry internally; exhaustion raises WriteNotAttempted, the terminal error for a never-attempted write.
entries.is_not: This is not an uncertain write; nothing could have been applied, so retry is safe.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried {operation} and the network never delivered it to Canvas: DNS or connection refused on every attempt. What the evidence showed: the provider demonstrably never saw the request bytes, so nothing was applied and this is the safe-to-retry case. What this means: the write simply did not happen. What happens next: I am releasing the claim and retrying the write cleanly once connectivity is back.
entries.auto_action: Release the claim, journal under a fresh event id, and retry the write.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate if the network failure persists, since that points at the egress path or a provider outage rather than the operation.
entries.signature_notes: classification: "WriteNotAttempted"; journal: "journaled under a fresh event id; claim released"; op_id: "reusable after claim release"; triggers: "provider-never-saw-it failures on every attempt (DNS failure, connection refused, unreachable host)"

entries.title: One dead session produces N uncertain writes (no sticky dead-session flag)
entries.root_cause: Verified: ChromiumSession has no sticky dead-session flag; every write after death re-attempts and journals another uncertain. No double-apply risk (Canvas refuses dead sessions), but the journal fills with uncertain entries instead of one loud stop.
entries.is_not: This is not N independent failures; it is one dead session observed N times.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I ran a batch against {tenant} and every operation after the first came back uncertain. What the evidence showed: the session died once, but the system kept trying Canvas for each later operation, recording a separate uncertain entry each time. What this means: you are looking at one dead session, not a string of bad operations. What happens next: I am stopping the batch at the first death, treating it as the standard re-sign-in flow, and reconciling the uncertain operations one by one rather than letting them pile up.
entries.auto_action: Stop the run on first SessionDead; reconcile uncertain ops individually via readback.
entries.escalate_when: Surface to the educator as a single session death, not as many failures; ask for the one re-sign-in.
entries.signature_notes: evidence: "W4-P2-2: two writes on one session object against a dead transport produced 2 provider calls and 2 UncertainWrites; no 'first detection stops the run' behavior"; pattern: "first op raises SessionDead, later ops on the same session object each re-attempt the provider and journal another UncertainWrite"

entries.title: Typo'd course_id hits a different existing course (no target-identity verification)
entries.root_cause: Verified: FrozenPlan requires field presence only; admit() and the write gates never read course_id from params, check the course exists, or confirm the course name matches intent. A typo that 404s fails closed; a typo that hits another existing course succeeds silently.
entries.is_not: This is not a provider error; every gate passed because the gates do not verify identity.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I am about to run {operation} against course {course_id} and I want to double-check the target with you first. What the evidence showed: the system cannot check on its own that this course number is the course you meant: a typo that lands on a different real course would succeed silently. What this means: I need your eyes on the target before any write goes out. What happens next: please confirm the course name and term for {course_id}; if a name looks right but slightly off (for example, a lookalike character), I will flag it explicitly before proceeding.
entries.auto_action: Require explicit educator confirmation of course name and term for write-class ops; flag confusable/homoglyph names and refuse to proceed without explicit confirmation.
entries.escalate_when: Always confirm the target with the educator before write-class ops on a course id that has not been verified this session.
entries.signature_notes: admission_record: "digests only, no readable tenant/course_id/course name for review"; evidence: "W4-P0-11, W5-P1-1 (injection), proven synthetically"; pattern: "frozen plan names course_id that passes every gate but is the wrong course"; post_fix: "homoglyph/confusable course names trigger a warning requiring explicit educator confirmation (NFKC + UTS-39)"

entries.title: Globally wrong tenant sails through all gates (tenant binding is self-consistent only)
entries.root_cause: Verified: the digest binding detects mint-A/dispatch-B, but cannot detect that A itself is wrong. If CANVAS_BASE is misconfigured to a typo'd tenant the educator then signs into, every write is approved for the wrong tenant.
entries.is_not: This is not a session problem; the session can be perfectly valid on the wrong tenant.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I noticed the configured tenant is {tenant} and I want to verify it is really your school before I do anything write-class. What the evidence showed: the system's tenant checks only confirm internal consistency: if the configured address was wrong from the start, every check would still pass. What this means: a misconfigured tenant would let me work on the wrong school's courses without any gate firing. What happens next: I am running the users/self readback so you can confirm the signed-in identity, and I need you to confirm the tenant address itself matches your school.
entries.auto_action: Run users/self readback; require the educator to confirm the tenant base matches their school before write-class dispatch.
entries.escalate_when: Always confirm the tenant with the educator on first setup and whenever the tenant config changes.
entries.signature_notes: evidence: "W4-P1-14, proven synthetically"; guard_gap: "cross-tenant retarget is refused (digest binding works), but a uniformly wrong tenant is not detected"; pattern: "approval minted and admitted with tenant_base=https://wrong-school.example.edu; every write 'correctly' approved for the wrong tenant"

entries.title: Crashing helper relaunched every 5 minutes forever (no circuit breaker)
entries.root_cause: Verified gap: there is no circuit breaker on helper relaunch; a deterministically crashing helper is relaunched every 5 minutes forever.
entries.is_not: This is not normal supervision; it is a stuck recovery loop.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I found the login helper crashing and being restarted every few minutes on a loop. What the evidence showed: the supervisor attempting recovery on every check without the helper ever staying healthy, which means something repeatable is killing it. What this means: automatic recovery cannot fix this one; the crash cause has to be found. What happens next: I am stopping the loop from churning and collecting the real failure from the helper logs so it can be diagnosed.
entries.auto_action: Break the relaunch loop (stop auto-recovery), capture server.log and the crash signature, and surface for diagnosis.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate to engineering with the captured logs; do not keep relaunching silently.
entries.signature_notes: evidence: "W5-P2-7 (resource); keepalive has quiet-window and cooldown for memory restarts but no failure circuit breaker"; pattern: "keepalive recovery fires every 5-minute tick indefinitely; helper never stays up"

entries.title: Keepalive diagnostics silently discarded (stderr to /dev/null)
entries.root_cause: Verified: an exec redirection bug sends the keepalive shell's stderr to /dev/null for the rest of the run, so when supervision itself fails there is no signal at all.
entries.is_not: This is not a helper failure; it is the supervisor failing silently.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I checked on the helper's supervisor and found it had failed without leaving any trace. What the evidence showed: a logging bug that throws away the supervisor's own error output, so a failing supervisor looks identical to a healthy one from the outside. What this means: the supervisor may not actually be watching the helper right now. What happens next: I am verifying the supervisor independently (lock state, last check-in, helper liveness) rather than trusting its silence, and fixing the logging so failures are visible.
entries.auto_action: Verify supervision independently of its own logs; fix stderr handling so diagnostics reach keepalive.log.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate to engineering: silent-supervisor failures need a human to confirm the fix landed.
entries.signature_notes: evidence: "W4-P1-10, demonstrated with read-only helper dir: exit 1, zero output anywhere"; mechanism: "keepalive.sh exec 2>/dev/null after lockfile open; every later diagnostic discarded"; symptom: "supervision failing with zero output; cron mails nothing"

entries.title: Disk-full upgrade destroys the tree while claiming successful restore
entries.root_cause: Verified: fail() only checks the backup dir exists, which is true for a partial backup, so the installer 'restores' a corrupt partial tree over the working one. Separately, final writes with 2>/dev/null || true mask disk-full truncation while exiting 0.
entries.is_not: This is not a normal upgrade failure; the recovery path itself is destructive.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I need to flag a serious problem with the last upgrade attempt: it ran out of disk mid-backup and then overwrote the working tree with the partial backup. What the evidence showed: corrupt files (many zero-byte) in the tree the installer claimed to have restored, while the intact original is still sitting in the failed-backup directory. What this means: the tree is damaged but recoverable from that backup directory. What happens next: I am not running anything else against this tree; the intact backup needs to be restored deliberately and disk space freed before any retry.
entries.auto_action: Stop all work on the damaged tree; preserve the byte-intact backup; require operator-driven restore and disk-space remediation.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate to engineering immediately; this is a stop-everything event with data-loss risk.
entries.signature_notes: evidence: "W4-P0-7: reproduced 2026-09-21; restored tree had 27 of 62 files corrupt (many 0-byte); byte-intact original sat in tree.failed-<ts>"; pattern: "backup hits ENOSPC; installer prints 'refusing to modify the tree' then 'restores' a partial backup over the good tree"; sibling: "disk-full final writes unchecked: installer exits 0 claiming success with truncated installed-manifest.json (W4-P0-8)"

entries.title: Live session store has no principal (first-seen pinning in reauth)
entries.root_cause: Verified: the live store predated principal capture, so reauth's exact-count and direct principal lookups failed (KeyError on canvas.principal, 6/10 drill failures). Fixed with first-seen principal pinning and subset ledger checks.
entries.is_not: This is not a session problem and not an account mismatch; it is a store-schema gap.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I ran the re-auth verification and found the stored session has no recorded identity from when it was first captured. What the evidence showed: the missing principal field in the live store, which is why the strict comparison failed rather than anything about your account. What this means: the first resume has nothing to compare against, so it pins your freshly verified identity going forward. What happens next: I am completing this resume with the live-verified principal pinned, and future resumes will compare against it normally.
entries.auto_action: Pin the fresh capture's live-verified principal on first resume; keep mismatch-refuses-and-escalates behavior thereafter.
entries.escalate_when: Surface to the educator the first time the pin is established, so they know the identity being pinned is theirs.
entries.signature_notes: evidence: "live-proof 2026-09-22 packaging fix; reauth drill 10/10 against the live store after fix"; fixed_behavior: "reauth pins the fresh capture's live-verified principal as the first-seen pin; mismatch still refuses and escalates"; state: "live session.json written by an older writer: no canvas.principal"

entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation} for the student the educator named. What the evidence showed: that name matched {match_count} roster entries at the {match_kind} identifier level, so no single student can be picked without guessing (reference {correlation_id}). What this means: I am not choosing one for you, because a silent wrong pick would attach the wrong student's data to this operation. What happens next: please tell me which student you meant: {candidates_public}.
entries.auto_action: Ask the educator to disambiguate using the listed candidates; re-run resolution only with an explicit choice (name plus section, login id, SIS id, or user id).
entries.escalate_when: if the educator cannot distinguish the candidates either, or the same query keeps coming back ambiguous (roster data quality issue to fix in Canvas)
entries.is_not: This is not a failure of the lookup itself: the roster read succeeded, and refusing to guess is the correct behavior.
entries.root_cause: Verified in code (learners/resolve_student.py): the identifier precedence ladder (user id, SIS user id, login id, email, exact name, fuzzy name) produced more than one candidate at its winning rung. Resolution is fail-closed on ambiguity.
entries.title: Student query matched multiple roster entries (ask the educator)
entries.signature_notes: classification: "StudentAmbiguous"; fixed_behavior: "never a silent pick; the agent-visible message lists candidates by stable label or section descriptor, never by name"; triggers: ["duplicate display names", "same name in several sections", "typo near two similar names"]

entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation} for the student the educator named. What the evidence showed: that name matched no active student enrollment in course {course_id} at any identifier level (reference {correlation_id}); filters skipped: {excluded_summary}. What this means: there is no student I can safely resolve this to, so nothing was looked up and nothing was changed. What happens next: check the spelling, or give me a stronger identifier (login id, SIS id, or email). If the student should be there, they may be inactive, concluded, in another section, or enrolled under a different name.
entries.auto_action: Ask the educator for a stronger identifier or confirm whether to include inactive/concluded enrollments or another section; re-run resolution with the confirmed scope.
entries.escalate_when: if the educator confirms the student is actively enrolled and the query still matches nothing (roster read or data issue)
entries.is_not: This is not proof the student does not exist: it is proof the query matched nothing in the active-enrollment pool that was searched.
entries.root_cause: Verified in code (learners/resolve_student.py): the full identifier ladder ran against every active student enrollment fetched for the course and produced zero candidates. State, role, section, and test-student filters run before matching, so stale records never shadow live ones.
entries.title: Student query matched no roster entry
entries.signature_notes: classification: "StudentNotFound"; fixed_behavior: "the no-match message reports which filters excluded candidates, so an inactive or wrong-section student is explainable, not mysterious"; triggers: ["misspelled name", "inactive or concluded enrollment", "wrong section", "nickname the roster never mentions"]

entries.title: Agent attempted to promote itself to edit mode without an educator-issued grant (ModeSelfGrantRefused)
entries.root_cause: Authority rule, enforced in code: only the educator can grant edit mode, and the agent can never promote itself. The admission gate caught the agent-side promotion attempt and refused it before anything was written.
entries.is_not: This is never a product bug, never a session problem, and never a misunderstanding about a timed grant. It is the agent violating the authority rule, caught and refused.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried to {operation}, and in doing so I attempted to move myself into edit mode without your grant. What the evidence showed: a self-grant refusal from the safety gate (reference {correlation_id}); no educator-issued edit grant was on file for this session. What this means: I tried to give myself edit permission you never gave me, which violates the authority rule; nothing was changed and no grant was issued. What happens next: tell me explicitly that I may work in edit mode, and I will proceed; until then I stay in plan mode.
entries.auto_action: Refuse the promotion; make no writes; ask the educator to grant edit mode explicitly.
entries.escalate_when: Always: a self-promotion attempt must reach the educator immediately.
entries.signature_notes: exception: "ModeSelfGrantRefused" (modes/ admission gate); the translator also sets the mode_self_grant_refused flag; dict evidence may carry either route.

entries.title: Write attempted in plan mode without an educator-approved validated plan (PlanModeWriteWithoutApproval)
entries.root_cause: Enforced plan-mode rule: plan mode is read-and-design only. A write requires an educator-approved, validated plan on file, and the gate refuses writes without one.
entries.is_not: This is not a missing edit grant and not a provider refusal; the plan itself was never approved.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried to {operation} while in plan mode, but there is no educator-approved validated plan on file. What the evidence showed: a plan-mode refusal (reference {correlation_id}); plan mode permits reads and design only, and no approval was recorded for plan {plan_id}. Nothing was written. What this means: planning is not permission; the plan must be validated and explicitly approved before any write can go. What happens next: review the proposed plan and approve it explicitly if it looks right, or grant edit mode so changes go without per-plan approval.
entries.auto_action: Refuse the write; keep the plan in draft; present the plan for educator review and explicit approval, or offer edit mode.
entries.escalate_when: Always: the educator must review and approve the plan, or grant edit mode, before any write.
entries.signature_notes: documented refusal shape (modes/ admission gate): exception "PlanModeWriteWithoutApproval" or dict evidence carrying plan_mode_write_without_approval; optional plan_id attr.

entries.title: Agent attempted to change a user setting without educator confirmation (ModeSettingsTamper)
entries.root_cause: Enforced ownership rule: user settings are educator-owned. Any agent-initiated change without an educator confirmation is refused by the settings guard before it applies.
entries.is_not: This is not a failed settings write and not a provider problem; the setting is unchanged because the confirmation was missing.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried to change the setting {setting_name} as part of {operation}, without your confirmation. What the evidence showed: a settings refusal (reference {correlation_id}); the setting is unchanged and the attempted change was dropped. What this means: settings are yours to change; I will not adjust them silently even when it would help the task. What happens next: tell me the exact setting value you want and I will apply it with your confirmation, or leave the setting as it is.
entries.auto_action: Drop the change; leave the setting untouched; never retry the change without explicit educator confirmation.
entries.escalate_when: Surface the first time a task reaches for a setting; the educator confirms or declines.
entries.signature_notes: exception: "ModeSettingsTamper" (settings/ package guard, workstream B); the translator merges the setting_name attr as evidence.

entries.title: Write refused: course resolution was ambiguous and unconfirmed (AmbiguousCourseWriteRefused)
entries.root_cause: Enforced no-guess rule: when course resolution returns multiple candidates or low confidence and the educator never confirmed the target conversationally, the write is refused rather than aimed at a guess.
entries.is_not: This is not a wrong-course typo and not a provider problem; the course exists, but the agent could not tell which one was meant.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried to {operation}, but the course target was ambiguous: the query {query} matched more than one course (or matched with low confidence), and you never confirmed which one. What the evidence showed: an ambiguous-course refusal (reference {correlation_id}); candidates seen: {candidates_public}. Nothing was written. What this means: I will not guess which course you meant; aiming a write at the wrong course would be silent damage. What happens next: tell me exactly which course this is for (name and term, or the course id), and I will run the write against the confirmed target.
entries.auto_action: Refuse the write; present the candidate courses side by side; run only after the educator names the target conversationally.
entries.escalate_when: Always: the educator must pick the course; the agent never picks for them.
entries.signature_notes: exception: "AmbiguousCourseWriteRefused" (modes/ admission gate); the translator merges query and candidates_public attrs as evidence.

entries.title: Write refused: destructive write needs the educator's explicit confirmation (DestructiveConfirmationRequired)
entries.root_cause: Destructive writes (HTTP DELETE, or entries marked destructive) are the one category that can still surface a confirmation inside edit mode while the educator's confirm_destructive_writes setting is on (off by default; edit mode does not ask per write unless the educator turns this guardrail on). The write was attempted without a recorded educator yes for that specific destructive action.
entries.is_not: This is not a mode-authority problem and not a provider problem; the educator is in edit mode and the write is authorized, but the destructive confirmation is missing.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried to {operation}, which destroys data. What the evidence showed: a destructive-confirmation refusal (reference {correlation_id}); your confirm_destructive_writes setting is on, and I have no recorded yes from you for this specific deletion. Nothing was destroyed. What this means: edit mode skips per-write approval, but destructive writes still need your explicit yes while that setting is on. What happens next: I will tell you exactly what will be destroyed and ask for your yes; I run it only after you say yes (or you can turn the setting off).
entries.auto_action: Refuse the write; the agent names exactly what would be destroyed and asks the educator for a yes; run only after that yes.
entries.escalate_when: Always: the educator must confirm the destructive action; the agent never destroys data on an implied yes.
entries.signature_notes: exception: "DestructiveConfirmationRequired" (modes/ admission gate); the translator merges entry_name and course_id attrs as evidence.

entries.title: Write refused: no confirmed course for this write (CourseResolutionRequired)
entries.root_cause: Enforced no-guess rule: a write that targets a course must say how that course was resolved (which course, how confident, whether the educator confirmed it). A write with no resolution, or with a resolution naming a different course than the write targets, is refused before anything is sent.
entries.is_not: This is not a provider problem and not a permission problem; the course may exist, but the agent has not shown which course it means.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried to {operation}, but I had not confirmed which course it is for. What the evidence showed: a course-confirmation refusal (reference {correlation_id}); the write carried no confirmed course, or named a different course than the one it targets. Nothing was written. What this means: I will not guess which course you meant; aiming a write at the wrong course would be silent damage. What happens next: tell me exactly which course this is for (name and term, or the course id), and I will run the write against the confirmed course.
entries.auto_action: Refuse the write; resolve the course with the educator conversationally, then re-dispatch with the confirmed course.
entries.escalate_when: Always: the educator names the course; the agent never picks it for them.
entries.signature_notes: exception: "CourseResolutionRequired" (dispatch/executor.py, mode-gated course writes).

entries.title: Operation refused: it declares itself a read but would change data (EffectClassMismatch)
entries.root_cause: Enforced integrity rule: the effect class comes from the operation's own requests. An operation that declares "read" (or "plan") but contains a PUT, POST, PATCH, or DELETE is refused, so a write can never skip write approval by claiming to be a read.
entries.is_not: This is not a Canvas error and not a session problem; the operation definition contradicts itself.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried to {operation}, but the operation is labeled as a read while it contains a request that would change data. What the evidence showed: an effect-class refusal (reference {correlation_id}); the dispatcher derives the real effect from the requests themselves, and they include a write. Nothing was sent. What this means: running it as a read would skip the approval every write needs, so it is refused. What happens next: I will not run this operation as defined. If you want the change it makes, I will prepare it as a write, and it will follow your current mode (plan mode asks for your approval first).
entries.auto_action: Refuse; never re-dispatch the same definition; offer the equivalent write through the normal write path.
entries.escalate_when: Report to engineering: an operation definition that contradicts its own requests is a defect.
entries.signature_notes: exception: "EffectClassMismatch" (dispatch/executor.py W4-P0-10, read-only block checks).

entries.title: Canvas stored something different from what was sent (WriteFieldMismatch)
entries.root_cause: Verified mechanism (D-009): Canvas can answer a write with success while storing different values. The executor reads the object back after every write and compares each requested field; a mismatch is recorded as a failed write with the fields named.
entries.is_not: This is not an uncertain write: the readback proved the stored values differ. It is not a success either.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried to {operation}. What the evidence showed: Canvas answered with success, but when I read the object back, some fields did not match what I sent (reference {correlation_id}); the journal names each mismatched field and the object's address. What this means: the change did not land as intended, so I am treating it as failed, not done. What happens next: I will show you what Canvas actually stored next to what was requested, and you decide whether I correct it, remove the object, or leave it as it is.
entries.auto_action: Record as a failed write; never report success; present requested vs stored fields and the object address for cleanup or correction.
entries.escalate_when: Always surface to the educator with the mismatched fields; they choose correct, remove, or keep.
entries.signature_notes: exception: "WriteFieldMismatch" (dispatch/executor.py post-write readback, a VerificationFailed subclass).

entries.title: Write sent, but no readback could confirm it (outcome: unverified)
entries.root_cause: Verified mechanism: after a write, the executor reads the object back to confirm it. When there is no readback route for the object, or Canvas does not echo the fields that were sent, the result is reported as "unverified": Canvas said success, and nothing independent confirmed it.
entries.is_not: This is not a failure and not a confirmed success. It is never reported as done-and-verified.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried to {operation}, and Canvas answered with success. What the evidence showed: I could not confirm the change with an independent readback (reference {correlation_id}); either Canvas offers no way to read this object back, or it does not return the fields I set. What this means: the change most likely landed, but I have not proven it, so I am not calling it verified. What happens next: please check it once in Canvas, or tell me how you would like to confirm it; I will not repeat the write, because a repeat could apply it twice.
entries.auto_action: Report as unverified, never as verified; do not re-dispatch; offer a manual check in Canvas.
entries.escalate_when: Surface every unverified write to the educator in the work summary.
entries.signature_notes: dict evidence: the executor result's "outcome": "unverified" relayed as {"write_outcome": "unverified"}.

entries.title: Unrecognized failure (structured fallback, never a shrug)
entries.root_cause: Contract, not a mechanism: any failure the catalog does not recognize must still produce a structured, evidence-grounded message and a preserved forensic record.
entries.is_not: This is not a license to guess the cause. The message states exactly what was checked and what is unknown.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation} on {tenant} failed in a way I do not have a classified pattern for, so I am reporting exactly what I know instead of guessing. What the evidence showed: the provider's response (status {status_code}, request id {request_id}), the session health (logged in: {logged_in}, browser alive: {chromium_alive}), the write-halt state ({write_halt_active}), and the transport's {attempt_count} attempts, all captured in the journal under {op_id} (reference {correlation_id}). What this means: I have ruled out the known failure patterns but have not identified the cause, so I will not retry anything that might have applied. What happens next: I am preserving the full evidence bundle for engineering review and parking the operation safely; you will get a concrete next step once the cause is identified.
entries.auto_action: Capture the full evidence bundle to the journal and engineering log; park the op; never blind-retry. If the op was write-class and possibly applied, reconcile via readback before any re-dispatch.
entries.escalate_when: Always surface to the educator with the evidence summary and the concrete next step; route the full bundle to engineering.
entries.signature_notes: contract: "this entry fires only when no other catalog entry's signature matches"; never: "never 'I don't know what happened'; never retry an uncertain write blindly"; required_capture: ["what was attempted (operation, tenant, object)", "full provider response (status, headers incl. x-request-context-id, body)", "session state at the time (logged_in, chromium_alive, write_halt_active)", "transport used and attempt count", "journal state (op_id, claim, receipt)"]

entries.title: No quiz matched the reference week (e.g. "last week's quiz")
entries.root_cause: Verified in code (query/quiz_resolve.py): "last week's quiz" means the ISO Monday-Sunday week before the current week in America/Chicago, matched on the quiz's effective date (assignment.due_at, then quiz.due_at, assignment.lock_at, quiz.lock_at, assignment.unlock_at, quiz.unlock_at, quiz.created_at). Quizzes with no dates at all are undated and excluded; unpublished quizzes are excluded. Zero candidates is a no-match, never a silent pick of the nearest quiz.
entries.is_not: This is not a failure of the lookup itself: the quizzes and assignments reads succeeded, and refusing to guess which quiz the educator meant is the correct behavior.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation} for {query}. What the evidence showed: no published quiz has an effective date inside {window_start}..{window_end} ({candidates_examined} quizzes scanned, {undated} undated, {unpublished} unpublished; reference {correlation_id}). Nearest dated quizzes: {nearest_public}. What this means: I cannot tell which quiz you meant without guessing, so I looked nothing up. What happens next: give me the quiz by name or tell me which of the dated quizzes above you meant.
entries.auto_action: Ask the educator to name the quiz explicitly (title or quiz id); re-run resolution only with an explicit choice.
entries.escalate_when: if the quiz should exist but has no due date in Canvas (data quality issue to fix on the assignment)
entries.signature_notes: classification: "QuizNotFound"; fixed_behavior: "never a silent pick; the agent-visible message lists scanned/undated/unpublished counts plus the nearest dated quizzes"; triggers: ["no due dates set on any quiz", "asking about a week with no quiz", "all quizzes unpublished"]

entries.title: Multiple quizzes matched the reference week (ask the educator)
entries.root_cause: Verified in code (query/quiz_resolve.py): more than one published quiz has an effective date inside the reference week window. Resolution is fail-closed on ambiguity.
entries.is_not: This is not a failure of the lookup itself: the quizzes and assignments reads succeeded, and refusing to guess is the correct behavior.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation} for {query}. What the evidence showed: {match_count} quizzes have an effective date inside {window_start}..{window_end}, so no single quiz can be picked without guessing (reference {correlation_id}). What this means: I am not choosing one for you, because a silent wrong pick would report the wrong quiz's failures. What happens next: please tell me which quiz you meant: {candidates_public}.
entries.auto_action: Ask the educator to disambiguate using the listed candidates; re-run resolution only with an explicit choice (title plus effective date, or quiz id).
entries.escalate_when: if the educator cannot distinguish the candidates either (duplicate quiz titles with different due dates)
entries.signature_notes: classification: "QuizAmbiguous"; fixed_behavior: "never a silent pick; the agent-visible message lists every candidate with title, id, effective date and date source, and points"; triggers: ["two quizzes due the same week", "duplicate quiz titles across weeks"]

entries.title: Failed-students query arguments are not valid
entries.root_cause: The failed-students query takes typed arguments (query/chain.py run_query): a quiz window of last_week or this_week, and at most one threshold (below_percent 0-100, below_points 0 or more, or letter_f). Any other value raises QueryArgumentsInvalid before any Canvas read.
entries.is_not: This is not a Canvas or session problem: the arguments passed to the query were not valid, so nothing was read.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation}. What the evidence showed: the query arguments were not valid ({evidence_summary}; reference {correlation_id}). What this means: I ran no Canvas reads and classified no students. What happens next: I will check what the educator asked for and run the query again with a quiz window of last week or this week and at most one threshold (a percent, a number of points, or a letter grade of F), asking the educator if their request is unclear.
entries.auto_action: Re-run with valid typed arguments; ask the educator when their request is unclear.
entries.escalate_when: never; this is a usage message, not an incident
entries.signature_notes: classification: "QueryArgumentsInvalid"; fixed_behavior: "no Canvas reads run on invalid arguments"; triggers: ["an unknown quiz window", "more than one threshold", "a threshold out of range"]

entries.title: The educator's time zone is not known
entries.root_cause: "Last week" and "this week" are the educator's weeks (query/chain.py educator_zone): the time zone comes from the educator's timezone setting, then the course's time zone in Canvas, then the educator's Canvas profile. When none of them names a zone, the chain raises TimezoneUnknown before it resolves any quiz; it never guesses a zone.
entries.is_not: This is not a Canvas or session problem: Canvas answered, but nothing names the educator's time zone.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation}. What the evidence showed: I do not know your time zone. It is not in your settings, the course, or your Canvas profile (reference {correlation_id}). What this means: I cannot tell which days count as last week, so I read no grades. What happens next: tell me your time zone (for example, America/Denver). I will save it as your timezone setting and ask the question again.
entries.auto_action: Ask the educator for their time zone, save it with `morrow settings set timezone <IANA name>`, and run the query again.
entries.escalate_when: never; this is a usage message, not an incident
entries.signature_notes: classification: "TimezoneUnknown"; fixed_behavior: "no quiz is resolved and no grades are read without a time zone"; triggers: ["no timezone setting, no course time zone, and no Canvas profile time zone"]

entries.title: "Failed" is undefined for this assignment (not_graded or no points)
entries.root_cause: Verified in code (query/thresholds.py): "failed" needs a fail threshold. not_graded assignments have no grade at all, and a null/zero points_possible makes a percent threshold uncomputable. The chain refuses to divide by zero or invent a threshold.
entries.is_not: This is not missing data: the assignment is configured in a way that makes "failed" meaningless.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation}. What the evidence showed: no meaningful fail threshold exists for this assignment (reference {correlation_id}). What this means: "failed" cannot be computed here, so no students were classified. What happens next: set a points value and a grading type on the assignment in Canvas, or give an explicit threshold like "below 40 points".
entries.auto_action: Ask the educator for an explicit threshold or to fix the assignment configuration; do not invent one.
entries.escalate_when: never; this is a configuration message, not an incident
entries.signature_notes: classification: "ThresholdUndefined"; fixed_behavior: "refuse rather than divide by zero or invent a threshold"; triggers: ["not_graded assignment", "points_possible null or 0"]

entries.title: Quiz reference the chain cannot resolve yet (named, yesterday's, or bare "the quiz")
entries.root_cause: Verified in code (query/quiz_resolve.py): the resolver only implements the "last_week" and "this_week" quiz windows. Any other quiz reference raises UnsupportedQuizRef instead of guessing a quiz. The typed query (query/chain.py) refuses other windows before calling the resolver, so this is reached only by a direct resolver caller.
entries.is_not: This is not a Canvas outage, not a session problem, and not an empty course: the quiz list was never consulted because the reference itself is not resolvable yet.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation}. What the evidence showed: the quiz reference could not be resolved ({evidence_summary}; reference {correlation_id}). What this means: this query only resolves the quiz due last week or this week so far; any other quiz needs the educator to pick it first. No students were classified and nothing was written. What happens next: ask the educator which quiz they mean (title plus due date from the course quiz list), then re-run for last week or this week as appropriate.
entries.auto_action: Stop without reading submissions; ask the educator to name the quiz; never pick one silently.
entries.escalate_when: If the educator names the quiz and the chain still cannot resolve it, escalate: the resolver may need the named-quiz lane.
entries.signature_notes: classification: "UnsupportedQuizRef"; fixed_behavior: "raise instead of silently picking a quiz"; triggers: ["named quiz reference", "yesterday's quiz", "bare 'the quiz'"]

entries.title: Failed-students read through the login helper failed (LiveReadError)
entries.root_cause: Verified in code (query/live_read.py, query/quiz_resolve.py, query/chain.py): every real API call in the failed-students chain runs as an in-page GET through the login helper's authenticated browser context. LiveReadError means one of those reads failed: the helper is down, its token file is unreadable or malformed, Chromium is not alive, the Canvas session is logged out or the principal check failed, a single read returned an HTTP error or non-JSON body, or a collection read was truncated. The chain is read-only; a failed read never writes.
entries.is_not: This is not a Canvas data problem and not a threshold problem: the chain never got far enough to classify any submissions, so an empty or partial class must never be reported.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation}. What the evidence showed: the live read failed ({evidence_summary}; reference {correlation_id}). What this means: the helper path that performs this chain's Canvas reads is unhealthy or one read was refused; no submissions were classified and nothing was written. What happens next: check the helper (process running, token file readable, Chromium alive, Canvas session logged in as the pinned educator), then retry the read. Never treat a failed read as an empty class.
entries.auto_action: Park the query; surface the read failure with the evidence; retry only after the helper and session are healthy.
entries.escalate_when: If the helper is healthy and the read still fails, or the principal check keeps failing after the educator re-signs in.
entries.signature_notes: classification: "LiveReadError"; fixed_behavior: "fail closed, never report a partial class"; triggers: ["helper down", "token file unreadable", "Chromium not alive", "session logged out", "principal mismatch", "read HTTP error", "non-JSON body", "truncated collection"]

entries.title: Query course is not a Canvas course number (InvalidCourseId)
entries.root_cause: Verified mechanism: the failed-students chain puts the course id into Canvas request paths, so it accepts only a plain Canvas course number. Anything else (a path fragment, a query string, text, an empty value) is refused before any request is built.
entries.is_not: This is not a Canvas error and not a permissions problem: no request was sent.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried to {operation}. What the evidence showed: the course I was given is not a Canvas course number, so I did not send any request. What this means: nothing was read and nothing in your course changed. What happens next: tell me the course by name, or by the number in its Canvas address (for example 12345 in /courses/12345), and I will run the query again.
entries.auto_action: Refuse before any read; ask the educator which course they mean.
entries.escalate_when: Never: the educator names the course and the query runs again.
entries.signature_notes: exception: "InvalidCourseId" raised by query/chain.py before any read.

entries.title: Canvas tenant not configured yet (first-run onboarding state)
entries.root_cause: Verified 2026-09-22: with no CANVAS_BASE and no browser lane state, ChromiumSession.load raises SessionMissing('chromium backend needs a Canvas base URL: ...'). This is the normal state of a fresh install before the educator connects Canvas, not a product defect.
entries.is_not: This is not session death, not a broken install, and not a Canvas outage. Nothing is misconfigured; the connection simply has not been set up yet.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried {operation}, but Morrow is not connected to your Canvas account yet. What the evidence showed: no Canvas school URL is configured, so there is no session to use. What this means: this is the normal first step and nothing is broken. What happens next: connect Canvas by telling me your school's Canvas URL (it looks like canvas.school.example.edu, with your own school in place of "school"), then sign in on the login helper page yourself. Once you are signed in I will verify it is really you and retry this for you.

Before this entry the case fell through to the unknown fallback with a parking message.

Nothing was sent and nothing changed. What happens next: I will resend the same change as a PATCH. If the PATCH write is not the one you approved, I will stop and ask first.

entries.title: New Quiz delete refused: never through the assignment endpoint
entries.root_cause: Guard rule, verified in code: guard_new_quiz_request refuses deletes through /api/v1 assignments paths; new_quiz_delete_request builds the quiz-API route.

What this means: the quiz was not deleted and nothing changed. The guard is protecting the quiz backend from becoming unreachable. What happens next: I will delete through the New Quizzes API route instead, with your approval as a destructive write.

entries.title: New Quiz stimulus write refused: stimulus is UI-only
entries.root_cause: Guard rule, verified in code: new_quiz_item_request in dispatch/executor.py refuses stimulus create/update targets; the New Quizzes contract doc records the provider 422.

entries.title: New Quiz settings write refused: saved settings block stale or unreadable
entries.root_cause: Guard rule, verified in code: new_quiz_settings_request in dispatch/executor.py refuses when the saved block is missing or unreadable; plan_new_quiz_settings performs the read-then-merge.

What this means: the refusal protected your existing quiz settings. Nothing was sent. What happens next: I will read the current settings block first, merge your change locally, and send the complete block for your review.

entries.title: New Quiz item update refused: interaction-id rename would orphan ghost stubs
entries.root_cause: Guard rule, verified in code: check_interaction_ids_preserved in dispatch/executor.py refuses added/removed interaction ids; the ghost-stub incident is recorded in knowledge/new-quizzes-contract.md.
entries.is_not: This is not a provider 400. The item on the quiz is untouched.

What the evidence showed: the guard refused the update: New Quizzes merges interaction_data by id, so regenerating choice, question, or blank ids does not replace the old elements, it orphans them into blank ghost-stub choices (observed in production: one item ended with 10 real choices and 18 blank ones). What this means: the in-place edit would have corrupted the item. Nothing was sent. What happens next: I will not do an in-place PATCH. The safe flow is delete the item and add the replacement, as two separately reviewed changes.
entries.auto_action: Do not retry the in-place PATCH; use the delete-plus-re-add flow with id preservation verified by check_interaction_ids_preserved.
entries.escalate_when: Surface whenever an item edit regenerates interaction ids, with the ghost-stub history stated.
